free_tier.stated: 50 GB Media Store per organization on the free tier, explicitly a HARD limit ('50 GB Media Store per organization (hard limit)'), plus 10 GB database storage per database. Pro raises Media Store to 250 GB then $0.05/GB-mo, database storage 10 GB then $0.80/GB-mo.
free_tier.notes: the headline offer as the seed recorded it; the binding constraint is in limits[]

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that no cap exists
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: no retention statement was extracted from the seed's quota and limits prose; absence here is a gap in this conversion, not a vendor claim that retention is unlimited
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Not separately metered; storage is the billed dimension. Serving via Deploy endpoints is capped by compute (up to 1 vCPU / 2 GB on free).

tooling: Python-native: `pxt.create_dir`, `pxt.create_table`, insert of images/video/audio/documents; the SDK is the client. Open-source core, so self-hosting is possible. No S3/WebDAV surface on the cloud tier.
chaining: Per ORGANIZATION, so org multiplication is the only route, and the docs frame 50 GB as a hard cap designed to stop exactly that. 10 TiB would need 205 orgs.
limits_note: 50 GB hard per org, 10 GB per database, 1 vCPU / 2 GB per database/service on free. The word 'hard limit' means there is no overage path at all — uploads fail rather than bill.
reliability_note: Small vendor; the product is really a declarative multimodal database rather than a blob store, so using it as bulk storage fights its data model (it wants typed columns, not opaque blobs).

extras.agent_focus: New and up-and-coming competitors to Hugging Face and ModelScope, judged on the hard test the brief sets: a credible HF competitor must permit multi-TB objects and generous per-account storage, because model weights and datasets routinely run to hundreds of GB / TiB. Split into three classes — Chinese domestic hubs (HF is blocked there, so a separate ecosystem exists), Western MLOps artifact stores (W&B/Comet/ClearML/Lightning/Deep Lake), and dataset-publishing startups (Source Cooperative, Oxen, OpenDataLab). Excluded and not re-reported: Hugging Face, ModelScope, Kaggle, Civitai, Ollama, Replicate, DagsHub, OpenML, fal.ai, Baseten, Modal.
